subject.title: fix(agents-bind): generate peer format for feishu group bindings

question: Which Feishu bind grammar should OpenClaw support before any candidate PR for the canonical Feishu bind issue lands?
rationale: The current public CLI syntax treats <channel>:<value> as an account id, but Feishu conversation ids need peer bindings; several open candidate PRs choose different compatibility tradeoffs.

options.title: Recognize Feishu conversation ids compatibly
options.body: Preserve account semantics for ordinary account ids while mapping recognizable Feishu conversation ids such as oc_* or typed chat/user values into peer bindings.

options.title: Add explicit peer syntax only
options.body: Keep channel:account unchanged and require a documented peer-kind syntax such as feishu:group:<id> for conversation bindings.

options.title: Accept the new account escape
options.body: Allow this PR's feishu:<id> reinterpretation and require users to move account binds to feishu:account:<id>, accepting upgrade churn.

recommendation.title: Recognize Feishu conversation ids compatibly
recommendation.body: Preserve account semantics for ordinary account ids while mapping recognizable Feishu conversation ids such as oc_* or typed chat/user values into peer bindings.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans public CLI docs, routing semantics, and current binding parser ownership where this history is strongest.
